title: CDC reports over 4,000 cyclosporiasis cases in 41 states amid outbreak - USA Today
snippet: # CDC reports over 4,000 cyclosporiasis cases in 41 states amid outbreak. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has upped the number of cases of cyclosporiasis to more than 4,000 in 41 states. A CDC outbreak update released Tuesday, July 21, reported 4,173 laboratory-confirmed U.S. cases of cyclosporiasis since May 1. More than 7,400 additional cases – many of them in Michigan and Ohio – have not yet been confirmed by laboratories, the CDC said. The number of states reporting cases grew to 41 in this latest CDC update, but these may not all be part of ongoing outbreaks. "Cyclosporiasis cases may not be limited to these states with known cases," according to the CDC update. The next day, July 18, the FDA said a Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce sample that was not part of the lettuce recalled by the company had tested positive for cyclospora.

title: Nearly 20 guests sick in cruise ship's third GI outbreak in two months - USA Today
snippet: # Nearly 20 guests sick in cruise ship's third GI outbreak in two months. ## The CDC is investigating a third gastrointestinal illness outbreak aboard a National Geographic cruise ship. Nearly 20 people got sick with gastrointestinal illness on a National Geographic-Lindblad Expeditions ship, marking the vessel’s third outbreak in less than two months. Among the 62 guests onboard, 18 reported being ill during the National Geographic Sea Bird’s July 10 voyage, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The news comes after two other outbreaks on the same ship during cruises in June and May. Both were caused by norovirus. The CDC has logged a total of eight outbreaks of gastrointestinal illness on cruises that met its threshold for public notification so far this year. There were 23 outbreaks that met that threshold in 2025, 18 of which were caused by norovirus, and it was behind 15 out of 18 outbreaks the year before.

title: Trump administration puts kibosh on HIV prevention funding - Roll Call
snippet: The Trump administration will not renew direct federal funding of community-based organizations that work on HIV prevention, according to multiple groups impacted by the freeze. The move is the latest step in the administration’s push to eliminate funding for DEI-focused initiatives that help the LGBTQ community. The Office of Management and Budget late last week told the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention that it will not renew $46 million in funding for the 96 community-based organizations to provide HIV testing, linkage to care, referrals for pre- and post-exposure drug treatment and outbreak response. Instead, the CDC is shifting resources to state and local health departments. Last week, the Trump administration put out a supplemental notice of funding to states encouraging them to give some money to the community-based organizations. HIV prevention organizations and advocacy groups are lobbying the Senate to propose more funding for HIV prevention and include language in their budget report guaranteeing direct funding to community-based organizations to conduct HIV prevention activities.

The Trump administration’s disruptions to a global AIDS relief program have forced organizations to close clinics, lay off staff and cut services, seriously impeding efforts to prevent and treat the disease in dozens of countries, a new report released Tuesday shows. But last year, it was impaired by the dismantling of the U.S. Agency for International Development and cuts to thousands of global health grants. “The disruptions were very widespread,” with services for young women, orphans and children impacted, said Elise Lankiewicz, policy associate for the nonprofit amfAR, The Foundation for AIDS Research, which released the report. Researchers contacted groups that got PEPFAR funding to deliver HIV services last year. Nearly a quarter — 166 groups from 46 countries — responded to an electronic survey conducted between last November and April, providing information on their funding, staff and services.
